chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best of them in executing them, and the most perceptive of them of them.'

He said: And he is the most knowledgeable of the people of Allah's affairs, the best of them for it, the most perceptive of it, the closest to Him, the most fearful of Him, the most loving of Him, the most grateful to Him, the most patient with Him, the most knowledgeable of it, the most capable of working for it, the best in speech for it, the most fulfilling of the covenant with Him, the most perceptive in working for it, the most capable of working for it, the best in speech for it, and the most fulfilling of the covenant with Him.

He said: Then he said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not create His creation except that they worship Him, and He did not send His messengers except to guide the people to His worship, and He did not send down His books except to guide the people to His worship.'

He said: And he is the most knowledgeable of the people of Allah's affairs, the best of them for it, the most perceptive of it, the closest to Him, the most fearful of Him, the most loving of Him, the most grateful to Him, the most patient with Him, the most knowledgeable of it, the most capable of working for it, the best in speech for it, and the most fulfilling of the covenant with Him.

He said: And that is because Allah, the Exalted, created the servants to worship Him, sent the messengers to guide the people to His worship, and sent down the books to guide the people to His worship. Therefore, the Imam is the most deserving of the people of worshipping Allah, the most knowledgeable of His affairs, the best of them for it, and the most perceptive of it.

key_terms.أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: Affairs of Allah (divine commandments and matters)

ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of the Prophets and Imams regarding their knowledge of Allah's affairs?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and *Fadilah* (superiority), asserting that the Imams possess the highest degree of gnosis (*Ma'rifah*) and moral perfection. This serves as a theological foundation for their authority as the exclusive interpreters of divine law, linking the purpose of creation—worship (*Ibadah*)—directly to following the most knowledgeable guide.
